Possible realizations of the theory and asymptoticapproximations are provided which permit to determine the fluid equations\textit{with prescribed accuracy.} As a result, asymptotic accuracy estimatesof customary LB approaches and comparisons with the Chorin artificialcompressibility method are discussed.

We study phonon-mediated transitions between translational levels of an atomin a surface-induced potential. We present a general master equation governingthe dynamics of the translational states of the atom. In the framework of theDebye model, we derive compact expressions for the rates for both upward anddownward transitions. Numerical calculations for the transition rates areperformed for a deep silica-induced potential allowing for a large number ofbound levels as well as free states of a cesium atom. The total absorption rateis shown to be determined mainly by the bound-to-bound transitions for deepbound levels and by bound-to-free transitions for shallow bound levels.Moreover, the phonon emission and absorption processes can be orders ofmagnitude larger for deep bound levels as compared to the shallow bound ones.We also study various types of transitions from free states. We show that, forthermal atomic cesium with temperature in the range from 100 $\mu$K to 400$\mu$K in the vicinity of a silica surface with temperature of 300 K, theadsorption (free-to-bound decay) rate is about two times larger than theheating (free-to-free upward decay) rate, while the cooling (free-to-freedownward decay) rate is negligible.

A number of giant HII regions are associated with soft diffuse X-rayemission. Among these, the Carina nebula possesses the brightest soft diffuseemission. The required plasma temperature and thermal energy can be produced bycollisions or termination of fast winds from main-sequence or embedded young Ostars, but the extended emission is often observed from regions apart frommassive stellar clusters. The origin of the X-ray emission is unknown.  The XIS CCD camera onboard Suzaku has the best spectral resolution forextended soft sources so far, and is therefore capable of measuring keyemission lines in the soft band. Suzaku observed the core and the eastern sideof the Carina nebula (Car-D1) in 2005 Aug and 2006 June, respectively. Spectraof the south part of the core and Car-D1 similarly showed strong L-shell linesof iron ions and K-shell lines of silicon ions, while in the north of the corethese lines were much weaker. Fitting the spectra with an absorbed thin-thermalplasma model showed kT~0.2, 0.6 keV and NH~1-2e21 cm-2 with a factor of 2-3abundance variation in oxygen, magnesium, silicon and iron. The plasma mightoriginate from an old supernova, or a super shell of multiple supernovae.

We present the results of a visible spectroscopic and photometric survey ofJupiter Trojans belonging to different dynamical families carried out at theESO-NTT telescope. We obtained data on 47 objects, 23 belonging to the L5 swarmand 24 to the L4 one. These data together with those already published byFornasier et al. (2004a) and Dotto et al. (2006), constitute a total sample ofvisible spectra for 80 objects. The survey allows us to investigate sixfamilies (Aneas, Anchises, Misenus, Phereclos, Sarpedon, Panthoos) in the L5cloud and four L4 families (Eurybates, Menelaus, 1986 WD and 1986 TS6). Thesample that we measured is dominated by D--type asteroids, with the exceptionof the Eurybates family in the L4 swarm, where there is a dominance of C- andP-type asteroids. All the spectra that we obtained are featureless with theexception of some Eurybates members, where a drop--off of the reflectance isdetected shortward of 5200 A. Similar features are seen in main belt C-typeasteroids and commonly attributed to the intervalence charge transfertransition in oxidized iron. Our sample comprises fainter and smaller Trojansas compared to the literature's data and allows us to investigate theproperties of objects with estimated diameter smaller than 40--50 km. Theanalysis of the spectral slopes and colors versus the estimated diameters showsthat the blue and red objects have indistinguishable size distribution. Weperform a statistical investigation of the Trojans's spectra propertydistributions as a function of their orbital and physical parameters, and incomparison with other classes of minor bodies in the outer Solar System.Trojans at lower inclination appear significantly bluer than those at higherinclination, but this effect is strongly driven by the Eurybates family.

Multifrequency VLBA observations of the final group of ten objects in asample of FIRST-based compact steep spectrum (CSS) sources are presented. Thesample was selected to investigate whether objects of this kind could be relicsof radio-loud AGNs switched off at very early stages of their evolution orpossibly to indicate intermittent activity. Initial observations were madeusing MERLIN at 5 GHz. The sources have now been observed with the VLBA at 1.7,5 and 8.4 GHz in a snapshot mode with phase-referencing. The resulting maps arepresented along with unpublished 8.4-GHz VLA images of five sources. Some ofthe sources discussed here show a complex radio morphology and therefore acomplicated past that, in some cases, might indicate intermittent activity. Oneof the sources studied - 1045+352 - is known as a powerful radio andinfrared-luminous broad absorption line (BAL) quasar. It is a young CSS objectwhose asymmetric two-sided morphology on a scale of several hundred parsecs,extending in two different directions, may suggest intermittent activity. Theyoung age and compact structure of 1045+352 is consistent with the evolutionscenario of BAL quasars. It has also been confirmed that the submillimetre fluxof 1045+352 can be seriously contaminated by synchrotron emission.

It is used the mechanical method of Abrikosov vortex stimulated dynamicsinvestigation in superconductors. With its help it was studied relaxationphenomena in vortex matter of high-temperature superconductors. It establishedthat pulsed magnetic fields change the course of relaxation processes takingplace in vortex matter. The study of the influence of magnetic pulses differingby their durations and amplitudes on vortex system of isotropichigh-temperature superconductors system HoBa2Cu3O7-d showed the presence ofthreshold phenomena. The small duration pulses does not change the course ofrelaxation processes taking place in vortex matter. When the duration of pulsesexceeds some critical value (threshold), then their influence change the courseof relaxation process which is revealed by stepwise change of relaxingmechanical moment . These investigations showed that the time for formatting ofAbrikosov vortex lattice in HoBa2Cu3O7-d is of the order of 20 microsec. whichon the order of value exceeds the time necessary for formation of a singlevortex observed in type II superconductors.

We show that the conditions which originate the spin and pseudospinsymmetries in the Dirac equation are the same that produce equivalent energyspectra of relativistic spin-1/2 and spin-0 particles in the presence of vectorand scalar potentials. The conclusions do not depend on the particular shapesof the potentials and can be important in different fields of physics. Whenboth scalar and vector potentials are spherical, these conditions forisospectrality imply that the spin-orbit and Darwin terms of either the uppercomponent or the lower component of the Dirac spinor vanish, making itequivalent, as far as energy is concerned, to a spin-0 state. In this case,besides energy, a scalar particle will also have the same orbital angularmomentum as the (conserved) orbital angular momentum of either the upper orlower component of the corresponding spin-1/2 particle. We point out a fewpossible applications of this result.

The status of 38 halo white dwarf candidates identified by Oppenheimer et al.(2001) has been intensively discussed by various authors. In analysesundertaken to date, trigonometric parallaxes are crucial missing data. Distancemeasurements are mandatory to kinematically segregate halo object from diskobjects and hence enable a more reliable estimate of the local density of halodark matter residing in such objects.  We present trigonometric parallax measurements for 15 candidate halo whitedwarfs (WDs) selected from the Oppenheimer et al. (2001) list. We observed thestars using the ESO 1.56-m Danish Telescope and ESO 2.2-m telescope from August2001 to July 2004. Parallaxes with accuracies of 1--2 mas were determinedyielding relative errors on distances of $\sim5$% for 6 objects, $\sim12$% for3 objects, and $\sim20$% for two more objects. Four stars appear to be toodistant (probably farther than 100 pc) to have measurable parallaxes in ourobservations. Distances, absolute magnitudes and revised space velocities werederived for the 15 halo WDs from the Oppenheimer et al. (2001) list. Halomembership is confirmed unambiguously for 6 objects while 5 objects may bethick disk members and 4 objects are too distant to draw any conclusion basedsolely on kinematics. Comparing our trigonometric parallaxes with photometricparallaxes used in previous work reveals an overestimation of distance asderived from photometric techniques. This new data set can be used to revisethe halo white dwarf space density, and that analysis will be presented in asubsequent publication.

It has been recently argued through numerical work that rotating stars with ahigh degree of differential rotation are dynamically unstable against bar-modedeformation, even for values of the ratio of rotational kinetic energy togravitational potential energy as low as O(0.01). This may have implicationsfor gravitational wave astronomy in high-frequency sources such as corecollapse supernovae. In this paper we present high-resolution simulations,performed with an adaptive mesh refinement hydrodynamics code, of such lowT/|W| bar-mode instability. The complex morphological features involved in thenonlinear dynamics of the instability are revealed in our simulations, whichshow that the excitation of Kelvin-Helmholtz-like fluid modes outside thecorotation radius of the star leads to the saturation of the bar-modedeformation. While the overall trends reported in an earlier investigation areconfirmed by our work, we also find that numerical resolution plays animportant role during the long-term, nonlinear behaviour of the instability,which has implications on the dynamics of rotating stars and on the attainableamplitudes of the associated gravitational wave signals.

Population structure induced by both spatial embedding and more generalnetworks of interaction, such as model social networks, have been shown to havea fundamental effect on the dynamics and outcome of evolutionary games. Theseeffects have, however, proved to be sensitive to the details of the underlyingtopology and dynamics. Here we introduce a minimal population structure that isdescribed by two distinct hierarchical levels of interaction. We believe thismodel is able to identify effects of spatial structure that do not depend onthe details of the topology. We derive the dynamics governing the evolution ofa system starting from fundamental individual level stochastic processesthrough two successive meanfield approximations. In our model of populationstructure the topology of interactions is described by only two parameters: theeffective population size at the local scale and the relative strength of localdynamics to global mixing. We demonstrate, for example, the existence of acontinuous transition leading to the dominance of cooperation in populationswith hierarchical levels of unstructured mixing as the benefit to cost ratiobecomes smaller then the local population size. Applying our model of spatialstructure to the repeated prisoner's dilemma we uncover a novel andcounterintuitive mechanism by which the constant influx of defectors sustainscooperation. Further exploring the phase space of the repeated prisoner'sdilemma and also of the "rock-paper-scissor" game we find indications of richstructure and are able to reproduce several effects observed in other modelswith explicit spatial embedding, such as the maintenance of biodiversity andthe emergence of global oscillations.

We explore the effect of an inhomogeneous mass density field on frequenciesand wave profiles of torsional Alfven oscillations in solar coronal loops.Dispersion relations for torsional oscillations are derived analytically inlimits of weak and strong inhomogeneities. These analytical results areverified by numerical solutions, which are valid for a wide range ofinhomogeneity strength. It is shown that the inhomogeneous mass density fieldleads to the reduction of a wave frequency of torsional oscillations, incomparison to that of estimated from mass density at the loop apex. Thisfrequency reduction results from the decrease of an average Alfven speed as faras the inhomogeneous loop is denser at its footpoints. The derived dispersionrelations and wave profiles are important for potential observations oftorsional oscillations which result in periodic variations of spectral linewidths. Torsional oscillations offer an additional powerful tool for adevelopment of coronal seismology.

It has been observed that particular rate-1/2 partially systematic parallelconcatenated convolutional codes (PCCCs) can achieve a lower error floor thanthat of their rate-1/3 parent codes. Nevertheless, good puncturing patterns canonly be identified by means of an exhaustive search, whilst convergence towardslow bit error probabilities can be problematic when the systematic output of arate-1/2 partially systematic PCCC is heavily punctured. In this paper, wepresent and study a family of rate-1/2 partially systematic PCCCs, which wecall pseudo-randomly punctured codes. We evaluate their bit error rateperformance and we show that they always yield a lower error floor than that oftheir rate-1/3 parent codes. Furthermore, we compare analytic results tosimulations and we demonstrate that their performance converges towards theerror floor region, owning to the moderate puncturing of their systematicoutput. Consequently, we propose pseudo-random puncturing as a means ofimproving the bandwidth efficiency of a PCCC and simultaneously lowering itserror floor.

The problem of limit shapes in the six-vertex model with domain wall boundaryconditions is addressed by considering a specially tailored bulk correlationfunction, the emptiness formation probability. A closed expression of thiscorrelation function is given, both in terms of certain determinant andmultiple integral, which allows for a systematic treatment of the limit shapesof the model for full range of values of vertex weights. Specifically, we showthat for vertex weights corresponding to the free-fermion line on the phasediagram, the emptiness formation probability is related to a one-matrix modelwith a triple logarithmic singularity, or Triple Penner model. The saddle-pointanalysis of this model leads to the Arctic Circle Theorem, and itsgeneralization to the Arctic Ellipses, known previously from domino tilings.

A detailed study of the geometries that emerge by a gravitating generalizedYang monopole in even dimensions is carried out. In particular, those whichpresent black hole and cosmological horizons. This two-horizon system isthermally unstable. The process of thermalization will drive both horizons tocoalesce. This limit is what is profusely studied in this paper. It is shownthat eventhough coordinate distance shrinks to zero, physical distance doesnot. So, there is some remaining space which geometry has been computed andidentified as a generalized Nariai solution. The thermal properties of this newspacetime are then calculated. Topics, as the elliptical relation between radiiof spheres in the geometry or a discussion about whether a mass-type termshould be present in the line element or not, are also included.

We present measurements of the infrared response of the quasi-one-dimensionalorganic conductor (TMTSF)2$SO3 along (E||a) and perpendicular (E||b') to thestacking axis as a function of temperature. Above the metal-insulatortransition related to the anion ordering the optical conductivity spectra showa Drude-like response. Below the transition an energy gap of about 1500 cm-1(185 meV) opens, leading to the corresponding charge transfer band in theoptical conductivity spectra. The analysis of the infrared-active vibrationsgives evidence for the long-range crystal structure modulation below thetransition temperature and for the short-range order fluctuations of thelattice modulation above the transition temperature. Also we report about a newinfrared mode at around 710 cm-1 with a peculiar temperature behavior, whichhas so far not been observed in any other (TMTSF)2X salt showing ametal-insulator transition. A qualitative model based on the coupling betweenthe TMTSF molecule vibration and the reorientation of electrical dipole momentof the FSO3 anion is proposed, in order to explain the anomalous behavior ofthe new mode.

The generation of oscillations in the microwave frequency range is one of themost important applications expected from spintronics devices exploiting thespin transfer phenomenon. We report transport and microwave power measurementson specially designed nanopillars for which a non-standard angular dependenceof the spin transfer torque (wavy variation) is predicted by theoreticalmodels. We observe a new kind of current-induced dynamics that is characterizedby large angle precessions in the absence of any applied field, as this is alsopredicted by simulation with such a wavy angular dependence of the torque. Thistype of non-standard nanopillars can represent an interesting way for theimplementation of spin transfer oscillators since they are able to generatemicrowave oscillations without applied magnetic field. We also emphasize thetheoretical implications of our results on the angular dependence of thetorque.

Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses reveal that the rubbed PTFE layers induce a high degree of molecular alignment in the overlying pentacene films. This study investigates the oriented growth of pentacene thin films on polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) layers deposited by vacuum evaporation and subsequently aligned using a rubbing technique. The molecular structure of the PTFEfilms was investigated by use of infrared spectroscopy. This oriented growth significantly enhances the crystallinity and grain size of pentacene, which are critical factors influencing charge transport properties. Using the coldfriction technique orienting PTFE layers with unidirectional grooves areobtained. The vacuum-deposited PTFE films serve as an effective dielectric substrate, with their surface morphology and molecular orientation tailored through controlled mechanical rubbing. The results highlight the importance of surface engineering of polymer dielectric layers to control the microstructure of organic semiconductors.

Utilizing the framework of open quantum systems, we derive the master equation governing the atom's dynamics under thermal fluctuations. These results provide deeper insight into atom-field interactions relevant for quantum optics and thermal quantum information processing. Our analysis reveals how the atomic population and coherence decay rates depend on the temperature and spectral properties of the radiation field. Inparticular, the time evolution of the number operator associated with the atomis given in terms of the probability of remaining in the first excited stateand the decay probabilities from this state by emission of field quanta offrequencies $\omega_k$. This paper investigates the time evolution of a quantum atom interacting with a thermal radiation field.

The Bogoliubov recursion is a particular procedure appearing in the processof renormalization in perturbative quantum field theory. By interpreting Bogoliubov’s recursion through the lens of Rota-Baxter operators, we offer an algebraic solution that unifies various renormalization schemes. We demonstrate that this extended identity naturally encodes the recursive structure of Bogoliubov’s renormalization procedure. Furthermore, we explore applications of the identity to the construction of counterterms and the organization of divergent integrals. In the classical, commutative, case, these identities can beunderstood as deriving from the theory of symmetric functions. Our findings not only enrich the theory of Rota-Baxter algebras but also provide practical computational tools for physicists working on renormalization. Our approach generalizes classical combinatorial identities to noncommutative settings, providing new insights into the algebraic structures underlying renormalization in quantum field theory. This work opens avenues for future research on the algebraic foundations of quantum field theory and noncommutative combinatorics.

We also explore the impact of isotopic and hyperfine structure on the line profiles and their polarization characteristics, revealing complex behavior that must be accounted for in precise diagnostics. Our results demonstrate that both D1 and D2 lines exhibit significant polarization signatures sensitive to magnetic fields typical of solar and stellar atmospheres. Here we present a detailed theoretical investigation on therole of resonance scattering and magnetic fields on the polarization signals ofthe Ba II D1 and D2 lines of the Fraunhofer spectrum, respectively at 4934 \AA\and 4554 \AA. We adopt a three-level model of Ba II, and we take into accountthe hyperfine structure that is shown by the $^{135}$Ba and $^{137}$Baisotopes. Notably, the D2 line shows a stronger response to weak magnetic fields due to its larger Landé factor, making it a valuable tool for detecting subtle magnetic structures. Employing advanced radiative transfer modeling that incorporates the Zeeman and Paschen-Back effects, we analyze the polarization signals generated in these resonance lines under varying magnetic field strengths and orientations. This work lays the groundwork for future investigations into the magnetic sensitivity of other heavy ion lines in the Fraunhofer spectrum. This study investigates the magnetic sensitivity of the Ba II D1 and D2 spectral lines within the Fraunhofer spectrum, aiming to enhance understanding of their diagnostic potential in astrophysical magnetic field measurements.

We explore potential implications for the broader neutrino sector and discuss the prospects for future investigations to confirm or refute the sterile neutrino hypothesis. Four-neutrino oscillations of the (3+1) type have been onlymarginally allowed before the recent MiniBooNE results, and become even moredisfavored with the new data (at the level of $4\sigma$). Our results indicate that the observed anomalies can be accommodated within certain ranges of mass-squared differences and mixing angles, though tensions remain with other short-baseline experiments. We analyze the compatibility of these findings with existing sterile neutrino hypotheses, examining the parameter space constrained by recent experimental data. Overall, this work underscores the importance of combined experimental and theoretical efforts to resolve the nature of neutrino oscillations beyond the standard three-flavor paradigm.

``Top--down'' models explain the observation of ultra high energy cosmic rays(UHECR; $E \gsim 5 \cdot 10^{19}$ eV) through the decay of very massive,long--lived ``$X$ particles''. Neutralinos, as stable supersymmetric particles, constitute a compelling candidate for dark matter and may be produced in exotic astrophysical processes at ultra-high energies. These findings highlight the potential of cosmic ray detectors not only to probe fundamental particle physics but also to shed light on the nature of dark matter through astrophysical observations. These neutralinos could in principle be detected. We demonstrate that under favorable supersymmetric parameter spaces, future experiments could achieve statistically significant detections within realistic observation times. We explore the signatures that distinguish neutralino-induced events from background cosmic ray interactions, focusing on unique features such as anomalous shower development and delayed secondary cascades. We investigate the prospects for detecting very high energy (VHE) neutralinos originating from cosmic sources in upcoming cosmic ray observatories.

This work enhances our understanding of the relationship between genome structure and function, providing insights into the mechanisms underlying gene regulation. Our findings reveal that chromatin folding is highly dynamic and correlates with functional genomic elements such as enhancers, promoters, and insulators. Utilizing advanced chromatin conformation capture techniques, we map the spatial architecture of the genome across different cell types and states. We identify key structural features, including topologically associating domains (TADs) and chromatin loops, that facilitate regulatory interactions. The GS polymer model is able to describe chromatinfolding in as well the highly expressed domains as the lowly expressed ones,indicating that they differ in Kuhn length and chromatin compaction. This study explores the three-dimensional organization of chromatin and its impact on gene expression, replication, and genome stability. We present evidence for different polymer foldingregimes of the chromatin fiber on the length scale of a few mega base pairs andon that of complete chromosome arms (several tens of Mb). Chromatin folding plays a critical role in orchestrating the complex regulatory landscape of the human genome.

The locationaccuracy achieved by the intelligent locator is comparable to that obtained bythe conventional triangulation method, while the applicability of theintelligent locator is more general since analysis of sonic ray paths isavoided. Results indicate a significant improvement in localization accuracy compared to conventional techniques, particularly in scenarios involving concurrent emissions.

Our results underscore the importance of off-plane surveys in uncovering the full extent of evolved stellar populations in the Milky Way. Analysis of the spectral profiles and velocity distributions suggests that these sources are predominantly asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars undergoing substantial mass loss. The spatial distribution and kinematic properties of the detected masers indicate their association with older stellar populations and possible membership in the Galactic halo or thick disk components. A signature of a warp of theinner Galactic disk is found for a disk subsample. Utilizing high-sensitivity radio observations, we targeted a sample of 150 infrared-bright sources identified from recent surveys, aiming to identify evolved stars exhibiting SiO maser activity beyond the main Galactic disk. Future high-resolution follow-up observations are planned to refine the distance estimates and investigate the physical conditions driving SiO maser emission in these environments. Our observations resulted in the detection of SiO masers in 42 sources, significantly expanding the known population of off-plane maser sources.

Although taste violations significantly affect the results of staggeredcalculations of pseudoscalar and heavy-light mesonic quantities, those enteringstaggered calculations of baryonic quantities have not been quantified. Our approach systematically reduces discretization errors, enabling more accurate extrapolations of baryon properties from lattice QCD simulations. This work paves the way for refined lattice computations of baryon structure and interactions, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of nonperturbative QCD dynamics. By integrating staggered fermion artifacts into the heavy baryon chiral expansion, we derive modified interaction vertices and loop contributions that account for taste-symmetry breaking at finite lattice spacing. This study presents a comprehensive formulation of Staggered Heavy Baryon Chiral Perturbation Theory (SHBCPT), extending the framework to incorporate lattice discretization effects inherent in staggered fermion formulations. The resulting chiral forms are appropriate to latticeresults obtained with operators already in use and could be used to study therestoration of taste symmetry in the continuum limit. The developed formalism provides a robust theoretical tool for extracting physical observables in baryon sector studies, facilitating direct comparisons between lattice results and continuum phenomenology.

We conclude that FeSt 1-457 represents a compelling example of a pulsating globule, providing new insights into the physical conditions governing core stability. Through spectral line modeling, we identify signatures consistent with oscillatory behavior, suggesting that FeSt 1-457 may be undergoing pulsations. Our findings challenge the traditional view of starless cores as quiescent objects and highlight the role of dynamical processes in early star formation stages. These motions appear to be subsonic andsignificantly below the escape velocity of the globule. Comparison of ourobservations with near-infrared extinction data indicate that the globule isgravitationally bound. We complement our observational analysis with numerical simulations of hydrodynamic oscillations in self-gravitating cores to interpret the observed velocity patterns. The simulations reproduce key characteristics of the line asymmetries and velocity gradients, supporting the hypothesis of a pulsating state. Future multi-wavelength observations and time-monitoring studies are recommended to further elucidate the nature and impact of pulsations in dense cores. The observed line profiles exhibit asymmetric features indicative of complex internal motions rather than simple static conditions. We discuss the implications of pulsations for the stability and evolution of starless cores, considering their potential to delay or trigger gravitational collapse.

We discuss the implications of our findings for understanding the large-scale structure of the universe and the ionization history of the intergalactic medium. By analyzing the cosmic flux decrement, we assess the validity and predictive power of these line-number evolution models. We compare simulated flux decrements with observational data to evaluate the consistency of each model. We compute, using numericalsimulations, the redshift evolution of D_A accounting for the presence of LyaForest absorbers and Lyman limit systems randomly distributed along theline-of-sight, and compute its intrinsic scatter at the 1-, 2-, and 3-sigmalevel due to fluctuations in the absorber properties (column density, Dopplerparameter, redshift) along different lines-of-sight. This work provides a framework for refining models of line-number evolution and improving interpretations of cosmic absorption features in future spectroscopic surveys. Our methodology involves simulating the intergalactic medium’s absorption effects on light from distant quasars and galaxies, incorporating different evolutionary scenarios. This result is independent to the form of the inputdistribution functions, and rather insensitive to the presence of high-columndensity absorbers, such as the Lyman limit systems.

This study explores the theoretical viability of wormholes serving as observational analogs or "foils" to black holes, aiming to elucidate their distinguishing features within the framework of general relativity. The implications of these results highlight the importance of developing refined observational strategies to identify potential wormhole candidates in astrophysical data. Thisis the case for: the apparently irreversible accretion of matter down a hole,no-hair properties, quasi-normal-mode ringing, and even the dissipativeproperties of black hole horizons, such as a finite surface resistivity equalto 377 Ohms. By analyzing metric solutions that permit stable, traversable wormholes, we compare their gravitational signatures and electromagnetic emissions to those of classical black holes. Our findings suggest that certain wormhole configurations can produce observational phenomena remarkably similar to black hole signals, complicating efforts to differentiate between these exotic objects.

We find that the multimodal color and metallicity distributions commonly observed in GC systems can be naturally explained by the radial changes in the host galaxy’s stellar population properties. Understanding the mechanisms whichlead to multiple globular cluster sub-populations is essential for a completepicture of massive galaxy formation. By assuming that globular clusterformation traces the total star formation and taking into account the radialvariations in the composite stellar populations predicted by the Pipino &Matteucci (2004) multi-zone photo-chemical evolution code, we compute thedistribution of globular cluster properties as a function of galactocentricradius. Our results suggest that GC multimodality is not solely a product of discrete formation events but also a consequence of continuous radial variation in the galactic environment. These findings provide new insights into the co-evolution of globular cluster systems and their host galaxies across cosmic time. This radial dependence reflects the complex assembly history of massive ellipticals, including in-situ star formation and accretion of satellite galaxies. We investigate the formation mechanisms of globular cluster (GC) systems in massive elliptical galaxies by exploring the radial variation of underlying stellar populations.

Our results provide new insights into the interplay between groupoid symmetries and E-theoretic invariants, facilitating computations in noncommutative geometry. We construct a framework that systematically relates equivariant E-theory for groupoid actions to their associated crossed product C*-algebras. This article develops an E-theoretic descent functor tailored for the category of groupoids, extending classical descent techniques in operator K-theory. Thelast section establishes the existence of the descent functor under a very mildcondition on $\Gamma$, the main technical difficulty involved being that offinding a $\Gamma$-algebra that plays the role of C_{b}(T,B)^{cont}$ in thegroup case.

By unifying these two fields, we address the limitations of traditional models that treat evolutionary processes and network structures separately. We present a new single-parameter model ofnetwork growth that unifies varieties of preferential attachment with thequasispecies equation (which models molecular evolution), and also with theErdos-Renyi random graph model. We analyze the magnetic and electronic structures to elucidate the coupling mechanisms between ferroelectricity and magnetism in this material. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the complex multiferroic behavior in TbMn2O5 and offer insights for the design of novel multifunctional materials. Our results reveal distinct temperature-dependent modulations in the scattering profiles, highlighting the interplay of spin and lattice degrees of freedom. We proposed that the low temperature incommensuratephase consists of the commensurate magnetic domains separated by anti-phasedomain walls which reduce spontaneous polarizations abruptly at the transition.

We investigate relaxation and dephasing of an electron spin confined in asemiconductor quantum dot and subject to spin-orbit coupling. This study investigates the phenomenon of spin dephasing arising from the accumulation of a random Berry phase in quantum systems. Numerical simulations corroborate the analytical predictions, demonstrating the impact of environmental fluctuations on spin dynamics. We develop a theoretical framework to quantify how stochastic variations in geometric phases influence spin coherence over time. Our analysis reveals that the random Berry phase introduces a distinct dephasing mechanism, which can dominate decoherence processes under certain conditions.

In spite of the large number of papers appeared in the past which are devotedto the lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods, basic aspects of the theory still remainunchallenged. This paper presents a novel lattice Boltzmann inverse kinetic approach tailored for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. Overall, this work provides a robust and efficient alternative for simulating incompressible fluid dynamics using lattice Boltzmann methods. By reformulating the kinetic model, the method directly recovers the macroscopic fluid velocity and pressure fields without relying on traditional pressure Poisson solvers. The proposed approach enhances numerical stability and accuracy, particularly in low Mach number flows, by systematically incorporating incompressibility constraints at the kinetic level. Possible realizations of the theory and asymptoticapproximations are provided which permit to determine the fluid equations\textit{with prescribed accuracy.} Validation against benchmark problems demonstrates excellent agreement with analytical and high-fidelity numerical results.

We find that simple power-law models tend to overestimate luminosities compared to more physically motivated disk models. We analyze a sample of ULXs observed with multiple X-ray observatories, applying a range of spectral models including power-law, multicolor disk blackbody, and combined models. Our results demonstrate that the choice of spectral model can lead to significant variations in the derived luminosities, with discrepancies up to a factor of two in some cases. Future studies should incorporate broadband spectral coverage and high signal-to-noise data to refine luminosity estimates. After considering foreground stars and knownbackground AGN,we identify four sources whose minimum luminosity exceed$10^{40}$ ergs/s, and call them Extremely Luminous X-ray sources (ELX). These findings emphasize the necessity of careful spectral modeling to avoid systematic biases in ULX luminosity measurements. This study investigates the impact of spectral model selection on the estimated luminosities of ultraluminous X-ray sources (ULXs). We also discuss the implications of our results for the classification of ULXs as intermediate-mass black holes or super-Eddington accretors. The estimated inner disktemperatures of the supersoft ELX are compatible with the hypothesis that theyharbor intermediate size black holes, which are accreting at $\sim 0.5$ timestheir Eddington Luminosity. Additionally, the inclusion of absorption and reflection components further modifies the inferred luminosity values.

We discuss the difficulties of predicting the solar cycle using mean-fieldmodels. Traditional empirical methods have provided limited predictive skill, motivating the exploration of physics-based approaches. Mean-field models, which parameterize the effects of turbulent convection and magnetic field generation, offer a promising framework for forecasting solar cycles. The first model represents a stochastically-perturbed fluxtransport dynamo. Solar activity, characterized by the periodic variation of sunspots, significantly influences space weather and terrestrial climate. The model incorporates nonlinear feedback mechanisms and variable meridional flow to capture key dynamical processes. This study investigates the potential of mean-field dynamo models to predict the solar cycle's amplitude and timing. However, uncertainties in model parameters and stochastic fluctuations limit precise cycle-to-cycle predictions. Through numerical simulations, we assess the model’s ability to reproduce past solar cycles and predict future activity. Furthermore, we show that evenshort-term prediction is impossible if there is a small discrepancy in theinput parameters from the fiducial model. Sensitivity analyses reveal that improved constraints on flow speeds and magnetic diffusivity are critical for enhancing forecast accuracy.

We present an experimental study of the dynamics underlying the buildup anddecay of dynamical nuclear spin polarization in a single semiconductor quantumdot. These findings provide critical insights for the development of spin-based quantum information processing and nanoscale spintronic devices. We investigate the dynamics of nuclear spin polarization in a single quantum dot influenced by the presence of a single confined electron. Utilizing time-resolved optical and spin resonance techniques, we demonstrate how the electron spin state effectively controls the polarization buildup and decay of the surrounding nuclear spins.

The estimation of missing input vector elements in real time processingapplications requires a system that possesses the knowledge of certaincharacteristics such as correlations between variables, which are inherent inthe input space. Computational intelligence techniques and maximum likelihoodtechniques do possess such characteristics and as a result are important forimputation of missing data. Neural networks offer a flexible, data-driven approach for imputing missing values by learning complex patterns in the data. This study investigates the effectiveness of neural network and expectation maximization (EM) techniques for handling missing data in various datasets. The results demonstrate that while EM performs well under assumptions of data distribution, neural networks exhibit superior adaptability and robustness in scenarios with complex missing data patterns. In contrast, the EM algorithm provides a statistically principled method by iteratively estimating missing values and model parameters to maximize the likelihood function.

The recently ratified IEEE 802.11e standard defines the Enhanced DistributedChannel Access (EDCA) function for Quality-of-Service (QoS) provisioning in theWireless Local Area Networks (WLANs). By modeling the system behavior through cycle time, we derive analytical expressions for key performance metrics such as throughput, delay, and collision probability. The proposed approach captures the stochastic nature of channel access and the impact of contention among different traffic classes. This study offers valuable insights for optimizing QoS provisioning in IEEE 802.11e networks and guides future enhancements in wireless MAC protocols. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy of the cycle time model in predicting EDCF performance under varying network conditions. This paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of the IEEE 802.11e Enhanced Distributed Coordination Function (EDCF) using a cycle time approach. The cycle time analysis is a simple and insightfulsubstitute for previously proposed more complex EDCA models.

The inclusion of three-body forces leads to a better agreement with experimental data for selected nuclear systems. The four-body bound state withtwo- and three-body interactions is formulated in Three-Dimensional approachfor identical particles as function of vector Jacobi momenta, specifically themagnitudes of the momenta and the angles between them. This study presents a comprehensive approach to solving the three-dimensional Yakubovsky equations for bound state calculations in few-body systems. Furthermore, the methodology developed here offers a flexible framework applicable to a wide range of few-body problems in nuclear and atomic physics. We extend the formalism by incorporating three-body forces, which are essential for accurately describing interactions beyond pairwise potentials. Our results demonstrate improved binding energy predictions and wave function properties in comparison to calculations limited to two-body forces. Thethree-body force effects on the energy eigenvalue and the four-body wavefunction, as well as accuracy of our numerical calculations are presented.

We investigate the foundational aspects of R-matrices associated with Rime, emphasizing their role in solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation. By establishing classification criteria, we facilitate the systematic study of R-matrices satisfying Rime properties. Solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation within the rimeAnsatz which are maximally different from the standard one we call "strictrime". Our approach integrates algebraic, combinatorial, and categorical techniques to classify and construct R-matrices exhibiting Rime-like features. Furthermore, we analyze the deformation theory of these matrices, highlighting their stability and potential applications in integrable models. Overall, this work advances the theoretical landscape of quantum algebra by illuminating the role of Rime conditions in the structure and classification of R-matrices. The results open avenues for future research into the applications of Rime-based R-matrices in mathematical physics and quantum computing. We discuss then connections of the classical rime solutions with the Bezoutoperators. The paper also discusses potential connections to combinatorial models and categorification efforts in quantum algebra. The interplay between Rime conditions and spectral parameters reveals new pathways for generating families of solutions with desirable properties. Anormal form of each individual member of the pencil depends on the discriminantof a certain quadratic polynomial. The research delineates explicit parameterizations of R-matrices compatible with Rime constraints, providing novel insights into their algebraic structure. Our findings contribute to the broader understanding of quantum integrable systems by revealing the significance of Rime conditions in the algebraic underpinning of R-matrices. This study explores the intricate structure of R-matrices within the framework of Rime, a class of algebraic entities characterized by their distinctive combinatorial and algebraic properties. We demonstrate how the Rime condition influences the symmetry and integrability properties of the associated quantum groups.

We analyze all X-ray timing data on 1E 1207.4-5209 in supernova remnant PKS1209-51/52 gathered in 2000-2005, and find a highly stable rotation withP=424.130451(4) ms and period derivative of (9.6 +/- 9.4)E-17 s/s. We present a detailed timing analysis of the X-ray pulsar 1E 1207.4-5209 based on a comprehensive dataset spanning multiple years. The measured period derivative is exceptionally low, suggesting a weak magnetic field strength relative to typical young pulsars. Our results provide new insights into the diversity of neutron star magnetic properties and their origins. The X-ray luminosity of 1E 1207.4-5209, L(bol) ~= 2E33 ergs/s at 2 kpc,exceeds its spin-down energy loss, implying that L(bol) derives from residualcooling, and perhaps partly from accretion of supernova debris. Additionally, the stability of the timing solution allows for precise constraints on the star’s braking torque and energy loss. Our study reveals a remarkably stable spin period, indicating that the neutron star has experienced minimal rotational irregularities since its formation.

We analyze the dependence of superhump period excess on mass ratio, confirming and refining existing empirical relations. Our simulations incorporate detailed treatment of tidal forces, viscosity, and thermodynamic effects within the disk. Differential motions in the fluid disccause converging flows which lead to strong spiral shocks once each superhumpcycle. Superhumps are periodic brightness variations arising from the interaction between the accretion disk and the secondary star. The modulation in total viscousdissipation on the superhump period is overwhelmingly from the region of thedisc within the 3:1 resonance radius. Our findings provide new insights into the physical mechanisms driving superhump phenomena and their evolution over time. The study further explores the impact of magnetic fields on disk morphology and superhump development.

Boolean Networks and their dynamics are of great interest as abstractmodeling schemes in various disciplines, ranging from biology to computerscience. We develop a theoretical framework to analyze how fixed external inputs influence the state evolution of nodes under asynchronous update schemes. This study investigates the propagation of external regulation within random Boolean networks and its impact on asynchronous dynamical behavior. Finally, we discuss the implications of our work for designing interventions in biological and technological networks subject to asynchronous updates. These findings provide new insights into the control mechanisms of complex systems modeled by Boolean networks, with potential applications in gene regulatory networks and neural circuits. All those variables in the network which are not directly fixed byPER form a core which contains in particular all non-trivial feedback loops. Our results demonstrate that the topology of the network and the logical functions assigned to nodes critically affect the reach and effectiveness of external control signals. Computational simulations corroborate the analytical predictions and reveal regimes where external regulation leads to robust convergence to attractors.

We determine the Z-module structure of the preprojective algebra and itszeroth Hochschild homology, for any non-Dynkin quiver (and hence the structureworking over any base commutative ring, of any characteristic). These findings offer new insights into the interplay between algebraic and arithmetic aspects of preprojective algebras. By employing techniques from homological algebra and noncommutative geometry, we extend known results from fields to integral coefficients. Our study provides explicit descriptions of these homology groups, highlighting their structural properties and connections to representation theory.

This work advances the theoretical framework necessary for exploiting BAOs as robust probes of dark energy and the expansion history of the universe. Our findings provide critical insights for interpreting BAO data from current and future galaxy surveys. Our results demonstrate that nonlinear effects induce a damping and slight shift in the acoustic peak position, which vary with redshift and cosmological parameters. When Fourier transformed, these out of phaseoscillations induce percent-level shifts in the acoustic peak of the two-pointcorrelation function. This study investigates the nonlinear evolution of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAOs) within the large-scale structure of the universe. Wediscuss why virialized halo profiles are not responsible for these effects,which can be understood from basic physics of gravitational instability. Utilizing advanced perturbation theory and high-resolution N-body simulations, we analyze the impact of gravitational clustering on the BAO signal over cosmic time. Additionally, we explore reconstruction techniques aimed at mitigating these nonlinear distortions to restore the primordial BAO signature.

By reconstructing the inverse \(f(R)\) functions, we demonstrate their capacity to mimic the effects of dark energy without introducing exotic matter components.

This paper presents a novel approach to multiple pattern matching by leveraging Markov chain models to analyze pattern occurrence probabilities. This Markov chain-based framework offers a robust foundation for advancing multiple pattern matching techniques in probabilistic and uncertain environments. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of our approach in diverse applications such as bioinformatics and data mining. We formalize, in a general framework, the concept ofMarkov chain embedding to analyze patterns in random strings produced by amemoryless source. Our method integrates probabilistic state transitions to accurately predict pattern matches, significantly improving upon traditional deterministic algorithms.

This study investigates the interplay between transverse and longitudinal responses in stiff polymer chains, highlighting the coupled nature of their mechanical behavior. Our findings reveal that the coupling effect arises from the intrinsic anisotropic stiffness and the nonlinear elastic properties of the polymers. Crossoverscaling laws and exact analytical and numerical solutions for characteristicresponse quantities are derived for different experimentally relevant setups.Our findings are applicable to cytoskeletal filaments as well as DNA undertension.

The nitrogen-vacancy (N-V) center in diamond is promising as an electron spinqubit due to its long-lived coherence and optical addressability. We investigate the polarization-selective excitation of nitrogen-vacancy (N-V) centers in diamond, aiming to enhance their optical control for quantum applications. The results are supported by theoretical modeling of the dipole interaction between the excitation field and the N-V center’s electronic states. We employ confocal microscopy combined with polarization-resolved photoluminescence measurements to characterize the excitation dynamics. We first apply this technique to N-Vensembles in [100] and [111]-oriented samples. This polarization control strategy offers a robust pathway for scalable quantum information processing and nanoscale sensing using diamond N-V centers. Our findings contribute to the development of more efficient and precise quantum devices based on solid-state spin systems.

For general quantum systems the semiclassical behaviour of eigenfunctions inrelation to the ergodic properties of the underlying classical system is quitedifficult to understand. We develop a rigorous framework to translate classical piecewise affine dynamics into unitary quantum maps, preserving key structural properties. The spectral characteristics and eigenfunction behavior of these quantum maps are studied to understand the emergence of quantum limits and their relation to classical invariant measures. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and the correspondence principle in piecewise linear dynamical systems. Our results reveal novel phenomena in the semiclassical regime, highlighting the interplay between discontinuities in the classical system and quantum ergodicity.

Our findings emphasize the necessity for rigorous controls and optimized protocols to ensure reliable localization and quantification of IDE expression. These insights contribute to improving diagnostic accuracy and advancing research on IDE-related pathologies. Insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE) plays a critical role in the metabolism of insulin and other peptides, making its accurate detection in tissues essential for understanding both normal physiology and disease states.

This study investigates the influence of stellar-mass black holes on the structural evolution of massive star clusters through a series of high-resolution N-body simulations. The presence of black holes also alters energy transport mechanisms within the cluster, leading to prolonged dynamical states distinct from traditional evolutionary pathways. Our results indicate that clusters hosting a significant population of stellar-mass black holes experience delayed core collapse and exhibit expanded cores compared to clusters lacking such remnants. These findings provide new insights into the role of compact remnants in shaping the long-term morphology and dynamical behavior of massive star clusters. We find that this does not result from the action of black holes,but can be reproduced by the effects of mass-loss due to rapid stellarevolution in a primordially mass segregated cluster.

In this work, we investigate the classification and manipulation of multimode Gaussian states under local operations, focusing on their standard forms. Counting arguments and insights from the phase-spaceSchmidt decomposition and in general from the framework of symplectic analysis,accompany our description of the standard form of pure n-mode Gaussian states.In particular we clarify why only in pure states with n<=3 modes all the directcorrelations between position and momentum operators can be set to zero bylocal unitary operations. We demonstrate the practical relevance of the proposed methods via explicit examples and discuss their implications for quantum communication and computation protocols. This study advances the understanding of multipartite entanglement structure and control in multimode Gaussian states, contributing to the development of scalable quantum technologies. By deriving canonical decompositions, we provide a systematic framework to characterize entanglement properties in continuous-variable quantum systems.

We compute the ground-state energies of a heavy-light K-Lambda like system asa function of the relative distance r of the hadrons. These findings contribute to the understanding of exotic hadronic states beyond conventional mesons and baryons. This study presents a comprehensive lattice QCD investigation of a five-quark hadronic molecule, aiming to elucidate its internal structure and binding mechanisms. Future work will focus on refining the calculations and comparing them with experimental observations to further validate the nature of these exotic states. The study offers valuable insights into the dynamics of multi-quark interactions and the formation of molecular hadronic states in QCD. The results indicate the existence of a loosely bound five-quark configuration, characterized by distinctive energy levels and spatial distributions. We hypothesize that an all light-quarkpentaquark may not exist, but in the heavy-quark sector it might, albeit onlyas an excited state.

The presence of millimeter to centimeter-sized grains in protoplanetary disks poses significant challenges to current models of dust evolution and planet formation. Utilizing a combination of observational data and numerical simulations, we analyze the conditions under which mm-cm sized particles can persist over disk lifetimes. These findings provide new insights into the early stages of planetesimal formation and the potential pathways leading to the assembly of planetary systems. In this paper, we address this conflict between theory andobservation, using more detailed theoretical models, including the effects ofsedimentation, collective drag forces and turbulent viscosity. Our results indicate that local pressure traps and reduced turbulence levels play critical roles in mitigating radial drift and promoting grain retention. However, if forsome reason the gas to dust ratio in the disk is reduced by at least a factorof 20 from the canonical value of 100 (for instance through photoevaporation ofthe gas), then the radial drift time scales become sufficiently large to be inagreement with observations.

Accreting T Tauri stars (CTTS) are observed to exhibit significantly lower X-ray luminosities compared to their non-accreting counterparts (WTTS), a phenomenon that challenges existing models of stellar magnetic activity. To explain this we have combined, for the first time, a radiativetransfer code with an accretion model that considers magnetic fieldsextrapolated from surface magnetograms obtained from Zeeman-Doppler imaging.Such fields consist of compact magnetic regions close to the stellar surface,with extended field lines interacting with the disc. Our analysis suggests that accretion-related phenomena, such as mass loading of magnetic loops and increased absorption by circumstellar material, play a crucial role in suppressing X-ray emission in CTTS. These findings enhance our understanding of star-disk interactions and have implications for the early evolutionary stages of stellar magnetic activity.

We develop a proof system that eliminates the need for the cut rule, thereby enhancing proof-theoretic properties such as consistency and decidability. Our approach builds on existing sequent calculi while addressing challenges unique to the interplay between intuitionistic and co-intuitionistic components. But hersubsequent ``cut-free'' sequent calculus for BiInt has recently been shown byUustalu to fail cut-elimination. This paper presents a novel cut-free sequent calculus tailored for bi-intuitionistic logic, a framework that extends intuitionistic logic by incorporating dual intuitionistic connectives.
